Following the dense real estate expansion that swept through the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again expanding its footprint in Sunnyvale. Here are the details.

Apple continues to expand its footprint

According to the Mercury News (republished by AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease an office building of 125,800 square feet at 580 North Mathilda Avenue in Sunnyvale.

This deal is Apple's first major real estate transaction in the area in 2026. Prior to this, the company spent over US$1 billion in 2025 expanding its footprint in the South Bay.

The expansion included the US$166.9 million purchase of the Cupertino Gateway complex consisting of three buildings, the US$350 million acquisition of the Mathilda Commons campus in Sunnyvale comprising two buildings, and the US$365 million purchase of the adjacent Mathilda Campus consisting of four buildings.

Apple subsequently spent another US$216 million to purchase two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its total Bay Area expansion investment announced in 2025 to over 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space.

Returning to Apple's new lease, the Mercury News noted that this deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay region begins to pick up, with vacancy rates improving compared to both the previous quarter and the same period last year:

Colliers reported that the office vacancy rate in the South Bay region was 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines the market area as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

The report also mentioned that, besides Apple, Amazon has also agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Road, also located in Sunnyvale.
